text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: "inference-api-prod - high 5xx rate during rollout" (PD# PD-987654)

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-987654 — 5xx surge in /v1/chat/completions across eu-west-2 canaries. Trigger: 10x baseline error rate.

sarah: seeing this in dashboards — error rate jumped ~0.2% -> ~11.8% on the new rollout group in eu-west-2. New revision: v2026.3-alpha-17, traffic 20%

devon: acked PD — I'm on it. Pulling canary logs now.

oncall-ml: ack (oncall). Loading perf traces and kvcache evictions.

sarah: stack traces indicate OOMs in runtime on a subset of hosts: "out of memory allocating KV cache frame" — looks like 2/10 nodes in the canary pool are throwing 500s, others show latency but succeed.

devon: pasting quick grep of worker logs:
```
2026-03-14T12:17:02Z runner-045 infer: ERROR: KV cache alloc failed: requested 512MB, avail 120MB
2026-03-14T12:17:03Z runner-045 infer: ERROR: request_id=7b2c... returning 502
2026-03-14T12:17:05Z runner-047 infer: WARN: high latency, gc spikes
```

ben: confirm: autoscaler added nodes earlier but some hosts are on older driver firmware; may cause different memory reporting. Rolling release uses heterogenous infra.

ops-lead: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause rollout (stop increasing traffic), 2) shift canary traffic back to stable, 3) reduce kvcache size via feature flag on canary. Which do we want now?

sarah: pausing rollout now would be safest. I can flip the rollout traffic back to 0% for v2026.3-alpha-17 and reroute to v2026.2-stable.

devon: trying command: `deploy-bot pause-rollout v2026.3-alpha-17`
deploy-bot: rollout paused for v2026.3-alpha-17 — traffic frozen at current split. (actioned by devon)

pagerduty-bot: PD-987654 acknowledged by devon (oncall). Escalation muted.

oncall-ml: can we quickly patch a runtime flag to reduce KV cache size on the canary hosts? That should reduce memory pressure while we investigate.

sarah: we have a feature flag `kvcache.size.limit` scoped to rollout groups. I'm pushing a scoped change to canary group: set to 256MB (from 512MB).

ben: note: if the flag doesn't propagate fast enough, we should evict the two bad hosts from load balancer. I can cordon runner-045 and runner-047 manually.

devon: running `k8s cordon runner-045 && k8s cordon runner-047` — cordon commands:```
kubectl cordon runner-045.eu-west-2
kubectl cordon runner-047.eu-west-2
```

ops-lead: please do that and then confirm health check recovery.

customer-success: FYI — support has one enterprise customer (Acme AI) reporting increased 5xxs for their production app. CS has opened a ticket and will update if they escalate.

sarah: cordoned both hosts. Observability shows error rate on canary traffic dropping within 3 minutes to ~1.5% after flag change and cordon. Latency normalizing.

devon: KV cache flag applied to canary group — confirmed on 6/10 runners. Propagation lagged on the cordoned ones, but cordon removed them from LB.

pagerduty-bot: PD-987654 status: mitigated — error rate reduced to <2%. Auto-escalation disabled.

ops-lead: next steps: 1) keep rollout paused, 2) run full vetting on infra drivers for runner images in eu-west-2, 3) schedule a rollback window if we can't get stable driver parity, 4) update release notes and postmortem if root cause is infra mismatch.

oncall-ml: handing off to ben for overnight monitoring. Ben — take ownership, please ack here when you pick up.

ben: ack — taking ownership. Will monitor metrics for 6 hours and coordinate with infra to check firmware/driver diffs.

customer-success: I've messaged Acme AI and told them we mitigated and are pausing rollout while we investigate. They'll wait for a follow-up in 2 hours.

devon: adding logs and timeline to incident ticket PD-987654. Will include commands used, cordon output, and flag diff.

incident-bot: Incident PD-987654 updated: status=mitigated, owner=ben, postmortem-required=true, severity=P2

ben: quick note for handoff: if errors spike again, immediate action is to route canary traffic to stable via `traffic-switch canary -> stable` and re-enable autoscaling constraints.

sarah: thanks team — great quick coordination. I'll open a follow-up thread for infra parity test plan. :thumbsup:"
